title: Department of Applied Chemistry — Master’s
organization: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
summary: Developed numerical methods and computational tools for quantum chemistry research.
description: Worked under the supervision of Prof. Henryk A. Witek, a Polish-born theoretical chemist specializing in quantum chemistry, applied linear algebra, and perturbation theory. All research communication and documentation were conducted in English.
Developed mathematical and computational tools for studying quantum systems, with a focus on electronic structure theory and numerical methods for solving multi-electron problems.

Designed and implemented numerical routines and simulation workflows that supported my master’s thesis Techniques for computing energy eigenvalues in quantum systems: sextic anharmonic oscillator and electrons on a 4D hypersphere (PDF), improving both computational accuracy and efficiency.

Implemented high-performance numerical computations primarily using Julia and Maple to handle symbolic expressions, algebraic manipulation, and large-scale iterative calculations, with Python and Linux tooling used to automate workflows and manage computational tasks.
Prepared the full thesis manuscript using LaTeX, integrating mathematical derivations, visualization outputs, and numerical results into a coherent scientific document.
responsibilities: Design numerical methods and simulation workflows for quantum-system research.
Implement and validate scientific computations across Julia, Maple, Python, and Linux tooling.
Document mathematical derivations and numerical results in a complete LaTeX thesis.
highlights: Completed a thesis on energy-eigenvalue computation for anharmonic oscillators and electrons on a four-dimensional hypersphere.
Combined symbolic computation, numerical optimization, automation, and technical writing in an English-language research environment.
